### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **82** documentable anchor(s).

**65** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (29 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (34 routes)`, `routeManager (23 routes)`, `userId (5 routes)`, `resolveRequestEnvironmentId (4 routes)`
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **15** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `54c4508c65e4f01803245cc9c2da68b36bce5b53` — the merge of head `a5de9d1e6e790b691b4a2f9fbb91f463fbbeddfe` into base `17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 54c4508c65e4f01803245cc9c2da68b36bce5b53 && git checkout 54c4508c65e4f01803245cc9c2da68b36bce5b53
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea a5de9d1e6e790b691b4a2f9fbb91f463fbbeddfe && git checkout -B drift-repro 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea && git merge --no-ff a5de9d1e6e790b691b4a2f9fbb91f463fbbeddfe

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 17566664299edac816b6672a673ac82b192d24ea` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6d576db52ec3e72f7312a74ecb257683652a5fd8`
Local-runs: probe — the narrowing face has no CI reading at this head that is both green and whole (two lanes red, the rest cancelled when the head moved), so the PR's own suites and the gates the dev re-ran after the main merge were run once in a throwaway worktree at 6d576db52: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/engine-banned-user-reference.test.ts` (9/9); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run src/security/user-assigned-work.test.ts src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts` (15/15); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run src/user-work-routes.test.ts src/rest-server-docblock-position.test.ts src/objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts src/rest-server-canonical-query-ast.test.ts src/write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts src/rest-write-response-internal-fields.tripwire.test.ts` (193 passed / 21 skipped); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/client exec vitest run src/admin-surfaces.test.ts` (10/10); `pnpm run check:route-envelope`, `check:adr-0087-registration`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:engine-double-contract` (all exit 0). Worktree removed afterwards.
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/validation-message.ts (the `reviewFace` hits) + the narrowing-face floor, every non-prose path of the diff: packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-banned-user-reference.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts, packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.test.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/core/src/security/second-object-read-exposure.pin.test.ts, packages/rest/src/user-work-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/user-work-routes.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-route-ledger.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-registrar-files.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-docblock-position.test.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server-canonical-query-ast.test.ts, packages/rest/src/objectql-slot-consumer-census.test.ts, packages/rest/src/write-route-hook-refusal-sentence.ledger.test.ts, packages/rest/src/write-response-internal-fields.tripwire.test.ts, packages/client/src/index.ts, packages/client/src/admin-surfaces.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces.dogfood.test.ts, scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + cited code read: packages/core/src/security/user-ban.ts (origin/main, #30287), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts `insert`/`update`/`count`/`getConfigs`, packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/types/src/response-envelope.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-milestone-summary.test.ts, docs/adr/0112, AGENTS.md step 3, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/lanes/spec.md`. Prose faces (`.changeset/30205-banned-user-work-handover.md`, `content/docs/**`) are the lane seat's ACCEPT, read here only for the declaration lines.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing, as the tree implements it.** `assertReferencesResolve` (engine-referential-integrity.ts) collects every caller-supplied, non-empty, non-object value of a non-`readonly` field whose `referenceTargetOf` is `sys_user` (a `lookup` to `sys_user`, a `user` field, a multi-valued member each on its own, a `master_detail` to `sys_user` too) that the existence probe resolved, then runs ONE `find` on `sys_user` (`$in`) under `{ ...context, isSystem: true }` and pushes a `reference_user_banned` entry for each id `isUserBanInForce` holds. Correct: the refusal is per field, per banned member, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with `fields[].code = reference_user_banned` (pinned by the objectql suite, 9/9 here). **Objects:** every object the engine writes, `sys_*` included — the write check has no platform-table exclusion, so a `sys_user_permission_set.user_id` grant to a banned user is refused too. The changeset's sentence ("a user field: the owner field, a `user` field, or a `lookup` to `sys_user`") covers that literally; the count/transfer half excludes `sys_*` on purpose, so the two halves are deliberately asymmetric. Judged correct, worth one clause in the changeset but not a defect.
2. **Write paths.** The check lives in `ObjectQL.insert` (single and array form, engine.ts call site 6824) and `ObjectQL.update` (by-id 8657 and predicate/multi 9093). That carries: `POST`/`PATCH /api/v1/data/OBJECT`; the batch door (`batch-routes.ts` calls `ql.insert`/`ql.update` per op); the import door (`import-runner.ts` writes through the engine's array-form `insert()`); a hook's `ctx.api` under a non-system context; a flow's `runAs: 'system'` write (keeps the check via `keepsFlowWriteReferenceCheck`). Exempt: any `isSystem` write without the flow mark (seed, install, restore, cascades), exactly as `reference_not_found`. The changeset's "every data write door" line is accurate.
3. **NEW assignment only.** The #29062 stored-row filter runs AFTER both pushes (`refused.filter(... stored.every(row => storedReferenceIds(row[r.name]).has(value)))`), so a value every targeted row already stores is forgiven for the banned code as well. Verified in code and by the suite ("a row that already holds the banned user stays editable") and by the dev's real-boot row (`200`). Reads are untouched (the check is write-path only). Correct.
4. **Fail-open on the ban read**, `warn` once, is the probe's own posture (an integrity check that cannot run must not invent a rejection). Correct and consistent.
5. **Cost of the narrowing: one extra `sys_user` read per non-system write that names a user.** This is real and it is what reds CI: three plugin-audit read-count pins (`audit-milestone-summary.test.ts:635` "a create pays ZERO reads" now `sys_user: 1`; `audit-option-label-summary.test.ts:563` `1` vs `0`; `implicit-reference-target-summary.test.ts:316/354` `2` vs `1`). The milestone test inserts `biz_deal` with `owner: 'usr_1'` under no `isSystem`, which is exactly the shape the new `find` fires on, and none of the 42 `main` commits merged into this head touches `packages/plugins/plugin-audit`, so this is the PR's red, not the base's. Must-fix (either fold the ban columns into the existing existence probe so the write pays no second read, or re-pin the three suites with the ruling recorded in them).
6. **`FieldErrorCode` gains `reference_user_banned`** (`errors.zod.ts`) with four locale templates (`validation-message.ts`). It is a published closed response vocabulary (`FieldErrorSchema.code`, `ui/action-params.zod.ts` `code: FieldErrorCode`), so the accept-set of the response schema WIDENS by one member: a consumer that switches exhaustively gains a case; nothing authorable moves (`Metadata-protocol: none` is right). The branch-information test of `lanes/spec.md` is met: a banned user versus a missing one is a branch a consumer acts on differently (offer the hand-over / pick another user). The regenerated `errors.mdx` matches (+22 more; the two lists).
7. **REST `user-work` family.** Both handlers: `resolveExecCtx` → `enforceAuth` (401 before any read; the dogfood matrix row `anonymous-deny-user-work` and its booted proof read, member controls 200 / 404 included) → `refuseUnknownQueryParams` (closed, empty set) → closed body (`toUserId`, `objects?`) → engine via `wiredEngineOrLoud` (501 when none). Count: one `engine.count(object, { where, context })` per (object, user-field) pair under the CALLER's context, `sys_*`/`managedBy`/disabled-package/`readonly`/`system`/phantom columns excluded, a thrown count names the object in `unreadable`, cap 200 pairs (`truncated`). plugin-security's authz middleware lists `count` beside `find`/`findOne`/`insert` (security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:448), so the count is RBAC/RLS-gated. Transfer: target read ONCE elevated inside the tenant (`{ ...context, isSystem: true }`, `USER_BAN_FIELDS`), refused `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`/`reference_not_found`, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`/`reference_user_banned`, or `400` same-user — all before any write (core and rest suites pin `update` not called); then per single-valued field `find(ids, limit=budget)` and one `engine.update(object, { [field]: toUserId }, { where: { id }, context })` per row under the caller's context — the ordinary path, so sharing, validation rules, hooks, approval locks and the reference check itself (the target is active) apply; failures are described through `handleRouteError` (the `/data` door's sentence, hook-refusal ledger row read), capped at 10 per field; ≤500 rows per call; `remaining` recounted per field. Envelope: `sendOk`/`sendError` only, `check:route-envelope` at zero (gate green here); every `code` used (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`) is in `ErrorCode`; the refusal carries `error.details.fields[0].{field,code}`. Judged correct.
8. **Cost and caps on the count.** Up to 200 `count` queries per call, for any authenticated caller, on any user id, with no memo and no per-route limit beyond the field cap. Bounded, and each query is one the caller could issue by hand through `/data`; acceptable for an administrator surface, recorded as a reading for the ui half (do not poll it).
9. **Observability of a ban.** Any authenticated caller who can write a user field, or call the transfer route, can now learn that a given user id exists and is banned (the reference probe already disclosed existence). This is the card's third bullet working as asked, not a leak of anything the ban dialog does not itself show; recorded so the ui half does not treat the code as secret.
10. **One ban predicate (#30287).** At this head `isUserBanInForce`/`USER_BAN_FIELDS` have one owner, `packages/core/src/security/user-ban.ts` on `main`; objectql imports them through `@objectstack/core` (exported at security/index.ts:182 on `main`), `user-assigned-work.ts` through `./user-ban.js`. No second `banned`/`ban_expires` predicate survives outside `user-ban.ts` in core, objectql or rest (grep at head). The dev's own copy was removed in 30927981. No drift.
11. **Census rows.** `REST_SERVER_REGISTRAR_FILES`, the route ledger (`sdk` rows with client methods present in `client/src/index.ts`), the docblock floor (6, sum 101), canonical-query floor 0, slot-consumer census 5→6, the second-object read-exposure classification, the internal-fields tripwire and hook-refusal ledger rows, the engine-double-contract pins: all read and all pass here.
12. **A misplaced docblock in `rest-server.ts`.** `registerUserWorkEndpoints` was inserted BETWEEN `registerSecurityExplainEndpoints`' docblock and its body: the explain docblock ("…`/security/explain`… D12 `manage_users`…") now heads the user-work registrar, and the new `[#30205] Register a user's assigned-work routes` docblock heads `registerSecurityExplainEndpoints`. The position pin only counts blocks, so it stays green. Must-fix, mechanical.
13. **Doc/skill authoring guard red at this head (PR-caused):** `authz-conformance.matrix.ts:322` carries `#30205` inside the runtime `note:` string of the new matrix row; the guard refuses a tracker id in a runtime string. Must-fix, mechanical (move the id to the comment above the row).

### ② Semver level

- Kind: `Metadata-protocol: none` — correct, nothing an author writes moves (`FieldErrorCode` is a response vocabulary; the ADR-0087 marker's own sentence says the same and `check:adr-0087-registration` accepts `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` at this head). Level follows the kind alone: `patch` on spec, core, objectql, rest, client; all five are `private: false` and all five carry the changeset. The BREAKING banner, the `!`, the single ADR-0087 marker and the `Skills-docs:` line are present. Level and marker: consistent with AGENTS.md step 3.
- Declaration: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is NOT whole. The diff widens the public face (a member added to a published closed enum, `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`), and `lanes/spec.md` and `landing-operations.md` make widening the public face clause ② (`放宽接受集或扩大公开面…即条款②`; `错误的 no 是可审计的假申报`), while a narrowing alone would not be. The closed pair allows one arm, and the arm that is BREAKING must stay, so the whole declaration is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset body. The tier this review serves is unchanged either way (the path arm `packages/spec/src/**` hits), so this is a declaration fix, not a re-review. Must-fix.
- Lane: `packages/spec` 恒归 `domain:spec`, but the spec lane pre-approves a gate-enforced, append-only vocabulary member when (a) the code's existence was ruled on the owning card (#30205, maintainer's word: "refused at the server"), (b) the fallback is unchanged and the clause-② path arm still goes through contract review (this record), (c) it is a pure append with no shape change. All three hold for `reference_user_banned` and its four templates; the pre-approval text names `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, and `FieldErrorCode` is the field-level sibling of that ledger (ADR-0114 D2), so I judge the edit acceptable in this lane under that class, with no spec-lane signature owed. The dispatch seat names this in ACCEPT.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none` in the dev report. No flag raised by the dev stands unanswered.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay for os-bill, `session_01Utp6CZavYYLh5k5r6jhgCF`); no external login to name.
- **Gates at this head.** The dev's 128/128 `dispatch-gates` reconciliation and the full dogfood battery (`os-verify-lock` exit 0, 419 files / 3496 tests) are pinned to `6e44006f`, BEFORE the merge of `main` (42 first-parent commits, among them #30287 which rewrote `core/security/index.ts`, `api-key.ts`, `resolve-authz-context.ts`, added `user-ban.ts` and three dogfood tests; #30307 in plugin-security; #30270 and #30432 in lint), the refactor onto `main`'s predicate (30927981) and the D6 marker (6d576db5). After the merge only seven gates and the targeted suites ran; the authz pair re-ran 139/139. **Unmeasured at this head:** the other 121 gate families, the plugin-audit suite (which CI shows red), and the full dogfood battery. review-checklist: for a `(narrowing)` PR the `dogfood_battery` line must be pinned to the head, full, red fixed. It is not. The battery must be re-run at the head that lands (the head has already moved to `ed851815`; the record there needs its own line).
- **Check-runs read on this head (REST API, 2026-11-05 ~16:00Z):** `Lint & Repo Gates` failure (required); `Lint · repo & tooling gates` failure (59/60, red: Doc/skill authoring guard, item ①13); `Test Core (5/8)` failure (plugin-audit 3 files, item ①5) and `Test Core` failure; `Dogfood Regression Gate` success is the attestation-verify step only — the three shards were `skipped`, so it measures nothing on a PR; the type-check, ESLint, dispatch-gates, Build Core, remaining Test Core/Test UI shards and Type Check UI were `cancelled` when the head moved, so they have no reading at this head. Green: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs, filter. The merge base `c045c341` is not the source of either red (the failing files are untouched by the merged commits and the assertion deltas are the PR's read).
- **`Fixes #30205` closes a card whose first two Expected bullets (the ban dialog's counts and the hand-over offer) are the `domain:ui` half.** The PR body says that half is "a separate `domain:ui` card", but the card's timeline shows no such card. review-checklist: landing only the implementable half ⇒ `Part of #30205`, unless the ui card is filed first and the maintainer wants #30205 closed by the server half. For the lane seat to settle before ready (not card-worthy on its own).
- The PR body's "Two-minute verification" line and the `objectql` sentence already name `core`'s `security/user-ban.ts (#30287)`; the body edit the dev report asks the seat to make is already in place at this head.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The narrowing** (declared face, no `hits` of its own beyond the spec pair): holds against the card's third bullet and the measured defect (`POST /data/asset_repair_ticket` with `assignee` = banned user answered 201). The placement — inside the write-time reference check, on the same terms as `reference_not_found` (caller-supplied, ADDED values only, system writes exempt, flow writes kept, elevated `sudo()`-shaped read inside the tenant, fail-open with a warning) — is the right seam: there is one owner for "a reference the caller named", and the ban predicate has one owner in core. Keeping a stored banned value editable is the correct trade (the alternative freezes every record the person held). Multi-valued fields refused per member is right. The one design cost is the second `sys_user` round-trip per write that names a user; the plugin-audit pins exist precisely to make such a cost visible, and they did. Either folding the ban columns into the existence probe's read (one round-trip, as the card's "one extra find" sentence could be made true) or re-pinning with the ruling in the test is acceptable; shipping with the pins red is not.
- **`errors.zod.ts` / `validation-message.ts`** against ADR-0114 D2 and their first consumer: a closed catalog gains a member whose meaning is distinct from `reference_not_found` and whose template names the field, the id and the remedy ("pick an active user") in four locales; `buildFieldError` is the first consumer and already takes the code through `r.code ?? 'reference_not_found'`; the `adr0112-ok: D6` marker is on the literal. Holds.
- **The `user-work` family** against the card's first two bullets: counting under the caller's context and transferring through ordinary updates is the right posture (the card asks for "across objects the administrator can read"; a transfer that elevated would move rows the administrator could not touch by hand). Excluding `sys_*`, `managedBy`, `readonly`/`system` fields is right (a grant is not work; provenance is not reassigned). Refusing a banned target before any write closes the loop with the narrowing. The caps and `remaining` make it repeatable. The rules living in `@objectstack/core` because rest cannot import objectql at runtime is a sound dependency decision and the only `engine.ts` touch is the four-line host literal. Holds, subject to ①12 (docblock) and ①13 (guard).
- Nothing in `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**` or `.claude/**` moves; no governed path in the file list (Governed Surface Queue Guard green).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-dvfr9q`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CbPxYq1wQmUNWvMZkC`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fix, each on its own line for the card:
1. Test Core red is the PR's: three plugin-audit read-count pins (`audit-milestone-summary.test.ts:635`, `audit-option-label-summary.test.ts:563`, `implicit-reference-target-summary.test.ts:316,354`) count the new ban-state `find` on `sys_user`; fold the read into the existence probe or re-pin with the ruling, and make CI green.
2. Doc/skill authoring guard red is the PR's: `#30205` inside the runtime `note:` string at `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts:322`.
3. `dogfood_battery` is pinned to `6e44006f`, before the `main` merge; a `(narrowing)` PR needs the full battery pinned to the head that lands.
4. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` → `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` in the PR body and the changeset body (the spec enum widens the public face).
5. `rest-server.ts`: the `registerSecurityExplainEndpoints` docblock now heads `registerUserWorkEndpoints` and vice versa; swap them back.

## Contract review (delta)
